newsitem.title: USA: Philip Morris not eyeing Miller sale -source.
newsitem.headline: Philip Morris not eyeing Miller sale -source.

text.p: Philip Morris Cos Inc had no plans to sell its Miller Brewing Co unit, despite market speculation that the U.S. tobacco and food company was looking for buyers, sources familiar with the company said on Monday.

Philip Morris shares closed up 3-1/2 at 122-3/8, buoyed by a report in Corporate Financing Week, a publication of Institutional Investor, which said the company was considering selling its brewing operations.
"Our strategy is to invest in Miller and to build on our core brands, especially Miller Lite," Nicholas Rolli, a company spokesman, told Reuters.

Rolli declined to comment on market speculation of an imminent sale, but he said the company had recently announced a series of initiatives to streamline the Miller organization and to restore growth there.
Rolli said the company had assigned two new advertising agencies to work on its Miller Lite and Miller Genuine Draft beers.
Operating revenues for Miller Brewing rose 0.5 percent in 1996 to $4.3 billion, but operating income declined 1.3 percent to $440 million, it said.

The operating company shipped 43.8 million barrels of beer in 1996, down 2.7 percent from shipments the previous year. The decline mostly reflected to softness in Miller's Red Dog and Genuine Draft beer brands, it said.
